rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, Tables 4-6, Figs 2-6 - the authors measured canopy reflectance (350-2500 nm) with a FieldSpec 3 spectroradiometer on 172 cotton plants graded 0-4 for leafhopper damage in three fields (Warangal, Coimbatore), plus leaf chlorophyll and relative water content, and regressed 24 indices against severity grade.
rows.notes: The study reports only detection/grading of leafhopper severity at the single-plant level: new indices LHI 2 and LHI 4 gave R2 of 0.461-0.850 against visual damage grades across three fields (Table 6), and infestation reduced Chl and RWC (Table 5). It does not identify affected areas of a crop (unit of measurement is one plant under a 33 cm target), does not test any farmer action, and reports no result on preventing or reducing further pest damage. Detection is a precondition of the claimed control effect, so Q2 is no and upstream is set. The discussion mentions site-specific control tactics only by citing Willers and Riggins (2010). Authors do note weaker index performance in Field 1 attributed to soil, weather, cultivar and growth-stage differences, and that Chl and RWC could not be sampled in Field 3, but these are limitations of detection results, not of the claimed control effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a ground-based hyperspectral detection study of leafhopper damage in cotton; it provides no evidence on pest control or damage prevention, only on detection of severity grades.
